17-112.r: President declares an area a 'Scheduled Area' (Fifth Schedule); he can also end or enlarge it after consulting the Governor.

17-113.r: President's address to Parliament is prepared by the Union (Central) Cabinet, which holds real executive power.

17-114.r: First President Dr. Rajendra Prasad → from Bihar; born 3 December 1884 in a village of Siwan district.

17-115.r: First President of independent India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, hailed from Bihar.

17-116.r: Dr. Rajendra Prasad → only one among options to complete successive terms: 1950-1952, 1952-1957, 1957-1962.

17-117.r: V.V. Giri → 4th President as an individual (1969-1974); 6th by tenure order (after Rajendra Prasad's three terms, Radhakrishnan, Zakir Hussain).
17-117.t: Individual order and tenure order differ: Giri is the 4th person but 6th tenure.

17-118.r: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy → the only President elected unanimously (unopposed); tenure 1977 to 1982.

17-120.r: Zakir Husain 1967-1969; V.V. Giri 1969-1974; Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed 1974-1977; Neelam Sanjiva Reddy 1977-1982.

17-121.r: Order: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (1977-1982) → R. Venkataraman (1987-1992) → K.R. Narayanan (1997-2002) → A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (2002-2007).

17-122.r: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy did not serve as Vice-President before becoming President; Radhakrishnan, Zakir Hussain and R. Venkataraman did.

17-124.r: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (sixth President) was twice Lok Sabha Speaker: 17 March 1967 to 19 July 1969, and 26 March to 13 July 1977.

17-125.r: Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was Lok Sabha Speaker twice before becoming President (elected unopposed, 1977 to 1982).

17-126.r: Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, second President (1962-1967) → called the 'Philosopher King' or 'Philosopher Ruler'.

17-127.r: V.V. Giri (fourth President, 1969-1974) → linked to the trade union movement; twice chairman of the All India Trade Union Congress.

17-128.r: 'Missile Man' → Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (11th President, 2002-2007), for work on ballistic missile and satellite launch vehicle technology.

17-129.r: Chief Justice M. Hidayatullah served as acting President from 20 July 1969 to 24 August 1969.

17-130.r: Odd one: Jawaharlal Nehru was Prime Minister; Rajendra Prasad, Radhakrishnan and Zakir Husain were Presidents.

17-131.r: Pratibha Patil → 12th President (25 July 2007 to 25 July 2012), first woman President; 14th by tenure order.

17-132.r: UPA candidate in the 15th Presidential election → Meira Kumar (not in options). In the 16th: NDA's Droupadi Murmu vs opposition-backed Yashwant Sinha.

17-133.r: Dr. Zakir Husain: Governor of Bihar (1957-1962), Vice-President (1962-1967), President (13 May 1967 to 3 May 1969, died in office).

17-134.r: V.V. Giri appeared in person before the Supreme Court (bench under Justice S.M. Sikri) in his election dispute; petition dismissed; he won on second preference votes.

17-135.r: Rashtrapati Bhavan designed by Edwin Lutyens; Viceroy House till 1947, then Government House; C. Rajagopalachari first Indian resident (21 June 1948).

18-001.r: Vice-President elected (Article 66(1)) by all members of both Houses of Parliament, by proportional representation through single transferable vote.

18-002.r: Article 66: all members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) elect the Vice-President; State Legislatures have no role.

18-004.r: Vice-President → elected by MPs of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha (Article 66(1)); not directly, not nominated.

18-006.r: 16th Vice-Presidential election (2022) electoral college = 788: 233 elected + 12 nominated Rajya Sabha members + 543 elected Lok Sabha members.

18-007.r: Both President and Vice-President are elected indirectly; but State Legislature members vote only for the President (Article 54), not the Vice-President (Article 66).
18-007.t: MLAs vote for President, not Vice-President; nominated MPs vote for Vice-President, not President.

18-008.r: Vice-President must be qualified for election to the Council of States (Article 66(3)) because he is its ex-officio Chairman (Article 64); also citizen, age 35.

18-009.r: Vice-President: ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Article 64); elected by members of both Houses of Parliament (Article 66(1)).

18-010.r: Rajya Sabha Chairman → Vice-President (ex officio); he presides over it but is not its member.
18-010.h: Rajya Sabha is chaired by an outsider: the Vice-President.

18-012.r: Vice-President is elected by MPs via proportional representation and single transferable vote (Article 66), not appointed by the President. Other statements true.

18-013.r: Vice-President must qualify for Rajya Sabha, not Lok Sabha (Article 66(3)(c)); removal: Rajya Sabha resolution by majority of all members, agreed by Lok Sabha, 14 days' notice (67(b)).

18-014.r: If the SC voids a Vice-President's election, his acts on or before the date of the decision stay valid (Article 71(2)); so only statement 1 is correct.

18-015.r: Vice-President: second-highest constitutional office (Article 63); no formal functions as VP as such; acts as President in his absence or on death, resignation, removal.

18-016.r: While acting as President, the Vice-President does not act as Rajya Sabha Chairman (Article 64), gets President's emoluments (Article 65(3)); if he resigns, CJI discharges President's duties.

18-017.r: Vice-President removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution (majority of all members) agreed to by Lok Sabha, after 14 days' notice (Article 67(b)); it starts only in Rajya Sabha.
18-017.h: VP removal starts in his own House, the Rajya Sabha.

18-020.r: Vice-Presidents with diplomatic posts: S. Radhakrishnan (Ambassador to USSR, 1949-1952) and V.V. Giri (High Commissioner to Sri Lanka, 1947-1951); K.R. Narayanan was Ambassador to China.

18-021.r: Held Vice-President's office: M. Hidayatullah (1979-84) and Shankar Dayal Sharma (1987-92); Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy were only Presidents.

18-022.r: First Vice-President → Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (1952-1962), not Zakir Hussain (second, 1962-1967). Also true: amendment Bills need special majority; constitutional cases need five judges.

18-023.r: Mohammad Hamid Ansari → 12th Vice-President, took office 2007, re-elected July 2012. First VP: S. Radhakrishnan (1952-1962).

19-001.r: Article 300 → the legal name of the Government of India is 'The Union of India'.

19-002.r: PM is appointed by the President, heads the Council of Ministers, and need not be an MP at appointment; Union executive power vests in the President (Article 53(1)), not PM.

19-003.r: PM is the real head of the Council of Ministers: Article 74(1) → Council headed by PM aids and advises the President, who acts on that advice.

19-004.r: Prime Minister is appointed by the President; other Ministers are appointed by the President on the PM's advice (Article 75(1)).

19-005.r: PM heads the Central Government (Head of Government); the President is Head of State (Article 74(1)).

19-006.r: Article 78 → PM's duties to the President: furnish information on Union administration; place a minister's decision before the Council if the President requires.

19-007.r: Constitution does not classify ministers into ranks (British convention). Article 75(1A) (91st Amendment, 2003): total ministers incl. PM not above 15% of Lok Sabha strength.

19-008.r: 91st Amendment (2003) → ministers incl. PM limited to 15% of Lok Sabha members (Article 75); same for States incl. CM (Article 164).

19-009.r: Cabinet = PM plus Cabinet-rank ministers only; a senior body within the Council of Ministers and the supreme decision-making body.

19-011.r: The word 'Cabinet' appears only in Article 352(3): President issues an Emergency Proclamation only when the Union Cabinet communicates it in writing.

19-012.r: Both false: Gopalaswamy Ayyangar report (1950) proposed grouping ministries, not a dedicated reforms minister; Department of Personnel (1 August 1970) was under Cabinet Secretariat, later Home Ministry.
